item.text: I’ll plan search, lending, returns, overdue tracking, and persistence as unfinished work, keeping the existing Node.js and JavaScript stack. I’ll make the remaining choices explicit in the setup package and have the plan independently reviewed.

# Review contract

Verification backends read this file: they receive it alongside the diff and are asked to name the principle a finding violates. Ordinary coding sessions do not read it.

A finding names the principle it violates. Name it and judge severity independently: the class governs blocking only, and it never lowers what you reported. A `blocking` class ADDS blocking to a finding already at critical or major severity. `major` and `suggestion` add nothing and leave your own decision untouched, so a finding the reviewer blocked on still blocks. `correctness` is a seventh value a finding may name and it blocks like security; it is the floor beneath the six, not one of them. Once capping is enabled, a finding inside this contract that names no principle is capped at suggestion.

## Outside this contract

accessibility, performance, data-safety

## Coherence

The change fits the design it lands in: one concept has one home, and new code follows the boundaries and data flow the project already has.

Violations: a second copy of an existing abstraction; logic placed in a layer the project keeps it out of; a reverse dependency between modules; a suggested ruling that applies and is not cited.

Blocking: major

## Uniformity

Same things look the same: naming, error shapes, file layout, and interfaces match the project's existing patterns.

Violations: a new naming scheme beside the existing one; an error returned where the project throws; a hand-rolled utility where a shared one exists.

Blocking: major

## Maintainability

The next reader can change it safely: intent is stated where it is not obvious, and the change is no larger or more coupled than its job requires.

Violations: a load-bearing decision with no recorded reason; a function that needs the whole file read to be changed; dead or duplicated paths left behind.

Blocking: major

## Robustness

The code behaves under the inputs and failures it will actually meet: bounds, absence, concurrency, partial failure, restart.

Violations: an unbounded read or loop; an absent value treated as zero; a write with no durability barrier where one is expected; a resource not released on the failure path.

Blocking: blocking

## Security

No new way for untrusted input or a less trusted party to act with more authority than intended.

Violations: unvalidated external input reaching a command, query, path, or privileged call; secrets or credentials in code or logs; a permission or sandbox setting widened without an explicit decision.

Blocking: blocking

## Quality

The change is verified to do what it claims: tests exist for the behaviour, they fail without the change, and the claim in the description matches what shipped.

Violations: a test that passes with the change removed; a green suite over code that is never executed; a description that names work the diff does not contain; a grep transcript in EXISTING.

Blocking: major

## Notes on this file

Ordering is load-bearing. The lens backend receives only the first 3000 characters of this file, head-truncated, so the six principles stay above anything this project adds. A principle pushed below that line is one a lens reviewer is asked to name without ever being shown it.

The "Outside this contract" line is read literally. Every line under that heading is split on commas and newlines into entries, trailing punctuation is stripped, and a `- ` bullet prefix is NOT stripped, so a bulleted entry matches nothing and prose written there becomes junk entries. One plain comma-separated line, or nothing at all. Entries are matched against a finding's category and, for a merged lens finding, against every contributing lens id.

A finding outside the contract is never capped and keeps the severity its reviewer gave it. Outside is therefore the LOUD side: the shorter the line, the more this contract covers and the more it quiets. An empty line is the widest coverage and the quietest gate, which is why `storybloq validate` warns about one. Silencing a category is a different mechanism and lives in `.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

The Outside line ships with three lens ids on it because the six principles above genuinely say nothing
about those subjects, and a finding is better passed through on its reviewer's judgement than capped for
naming no principle. Remove an entry to bring that subject under the contract; add one, as a category
string or a lens id, to take a subject out. Do not use this line to silence a category: a finding outside
the contract keeps the severity its reviewer gave it, which is louder, not quieter. Silencing lives in
`.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

Review id: R1
Independently review this complete Storybloq setup plan for coverage, fidelity, journey usability, ticket boundaries/dependencies, feasibility, domain/privacy correctness and verification. Return only JSON with verdict (string) and findings (array of strings). Do not write files or execute tests/build/install/server. This is planning only.

Sources: README.md describes Shelfmate, a school book-room catalogue, with search and lending incorrectly claimed complete and overdue/persistence outstanding. src/books.js implements in-memory listBooks/addBook with title validation and numeric ids; src/server.js provides GET/POST /books on port 3000; test/books.test.js has one node:test test for addition. package.json: JavaScript ES modules, no dependencies, scripts start=node src/server.js and test=node --test. No git repository or .story or governance files. No tests have been run during setup. User corrected README: plan absent search/lending. User requirements: one teacher only, pupils never use app; first version finds books, lends to a pupil, records returns, shows overdue books, loses nothing on restart; keep technology; use judgment for remaining choices.

Product outcome: teacher completes this journey through a small browser UI served by the existing Node HTTP server. Retain dependency-free Node.js/JavaScript; use plain HTML/CSS/JS and built-in filesystem JSON persistence. Assumptions proposed for approval: single process on teacher's machine, server bound to loopback, no accounts or network deployment; one book record is one lendable physical copy; minimal pupil label entered by teacher (no pupil accounts, directory or extra personal data); teacher chooses due date with editable 14-calendar-day default; overdue means outstanding and due date earlier than current local calendar date (not overdue on due date). These are chosen defaults, not source requirements. No reserved books, fines, reminders, reports or multiuser/cloud scope. Persistence protects acknowledged mutations across restart, preserves ids and outstanding loans, rejects corruption without overwriting, serializes writes with atomic replacement/durability handling and reports failed writes without committing in-memory success. Power-loss guarantees depend on filesystem and must not be overstated; verify the designed crash/restart boundaries. Runtime data under data/ excluded from git.

Milestone 1 durable searchable catalogue. Milestone 2 teacher circulation and overdue view. Milestone 3 verified first-version acceptance. Keep init's p0 Setup first. Tickets below use aliases, actual ids allocated only after approval. Every implementation ticket has the following complete description:

E1 Existing list/add catalogue (milestone 1, complete based on code inspection ONLY, no claim tests passed). Outcome: list/add books, from README and src/books.js/server.js. Scope: current in-memory module and GET/POST endpoints. Excludes: durability, robust input handling, UI, search and loans. Acceptance: source implements list/add with identifiers. Behaviour: missing title throws; this is evidence of current code, not desirable API handling. Verification: cited files and existing test/books.test.js inspected, not executed. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: none.

A1 Durable catalogue and safe HTTP handling (milestone 1, no blockers). Outcome: added catalogue survives restart, from user persistence requirement. Scope: JSON repository, persisted schema for books and next id, serialized atomic mutations, injectable storage for tests, request parsing/validation/error responses, loopback binding, bounded input, data path documented. Excludes: loan records/UI and authentication. Acceptance: successful POST survives restart; identifiers remain unique; malformed JSON or invalid fields yields 4xx without process exit; storage failure yields explicit failure without success or partial state; corrupt stored data stops startup safely without erasure; missing data file initializes empty only. Behaviour: empty list supported, clear startup/storage errors, retry safe against partial failed writes, escaped UI data later in A2; no accessibility surface. Verification: node:test temp-directory restart, write-failure, corruption and concurrent-write tests plus HTTP input/error tests. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: single process/local filesystem as above.

A2 Searchable teacher catalogue UI (milestone 1, blocked by A1). Outcome: teacher finds a book by title or author and can add a copy, from README search and user first-version journey. Scope: case-insensitive title/author search, GET filtering, plain accessible browser catalogue and add form served by existing server. Excludes: loans/overdue and UI frameworks. Acceptance: title/author matches shown, blank query lists all, no results distinct from empty catalogue, created book appears and persists, each row identifiable as a copy. Behaviour: labelled inputs, keyboard operation, visible focus and feedback, loading/empty/no-results/error/retry states, render user text safely. Verification: node:test search/API cases, teacher keyboard/manual journey. Prerequisites: A1. Assumptions: plain browser UI as above.

C1 Checkpoint: teacher reviews catalogue (milestone 1, blocked by A2). Question: Is finding and identifying a physical copy and adding one understandable? Artifact: working local catalogue/add/search screen. This gates B2's interaction design only; backend B1 and overdue B3 can proceed independently.

B1 Durable lending and return API (milestone 2, blocked by A1). Outcome: lend a copy to a pupil and record its return, from user. Scope: active/returned loan records, minimal pupil label, loan date/due date/return timestamp, schema upgrade preserving existing books, persistent loan identifiers, shared storage transaction boundary, lend and return HTTP actions. Excludes: pupil accounts, fees and UI. Acceptance: only one active loan per copy; unknown book/loan and invalid pupil/date rejected; lend/return persists before success; repeated return is harmless and does not change first return time; returned copy can be lent again; existing catalogue migrates without data loss. Behaviour: clear invalid/conflict/storage errors; same-copy concurrent lending accepts at most one; failed writes leave prior state; never expose pupil data in generic logs. Verification: node:test state-transition/date-validation/repeated-return/concurrency/migration/restart tests. Prerequisites: A1. Assumptions: one record per copy, editable 14-day default, date-only due dates and local calendar semantics.

B2 Teacher lend/return controls (milestone 2, blocked by B1,A2,C1). Outcome: teacher performs circulation without API tools, from user journey. Scope: availability, pupil-label/due-date lend form, active-loan details and return control in catalogue. Excludes: pupil login and overdue screen. Acceptance: find available copy, lend it, see its borrower/due date, return it, lend again; status survives browser refresh. Behaviour: disable repeated submission while pending; labelled keyboard-accessible controls and announced outcomes; retain inputs on failure, refresh on stale conflict, retry recovery. Verification: API integration tests and teacher manual keyboard journey including failure/refresh. Prerequisites: B1,A2,C1. Assumptions: minimal pupil label.

B3 Overdue list (milestone 2, blocked by B1,A2). Outcome: teacher sees overdue outstanding loans with book, pupil label and due date, from user/README. Scope: overdue query and accessible UI linked from catalogue, oldest-due ordering; date provider injectable. Excludes: reminders/fines and a separate return flow (existing catalogue return used once B2 lands). Acceptance: excludes returned loans and loans due today/future, includes outstanding loans due before local today, empty view explicit, view refreshes after return. Behaviour: labelled table/list and navigation, loading/error/retry, safe text rendering. Verification: node:test date boundary/month/year and returned-loan filtering cases plus manual UI keyboard verification. Prerequisites: B1,A2. Assumptions: local date semantics described above.

C2 Checkpoint: teacher demonstrates circulation (milestone 2, blocked by B2,B3). Criteria: find copy, lend to pupil with selected due date, see overdue record using representative past-due fixture, return it, confirm disappearance and availability. Artifact: working app using fictional pupil labels. Only final acceptance waits on this checkpoint.

D1 Restart and recovery acceptance evidence (milestone 3, blocked by A2,B2,B3). Outcome: first-version journey demonstrably survives restart, from user. Scope: end-to-end HTTP/restart tests, safe fixture isolation, whole-journey failure/recovery tests, README corrected with run/test/local-use/data-location/backup and restore instructions, document minimal retention handling for stored pupil labels and local-access boundary. Excludes: remote deployment, new backup service and extra product features. Acceptance: catalogue, active loans, due dates and recorded returns remain after stop/restart; corrupt storage leaves original bytes intact; failed saves never show false success; documented backup/restore preserves state; realistic demo uses only fictional pupil data. Behaviour: actionable recovery documentation without automatic destructive resets; tests clean temp data only. Verification: npm test plus manual browser journey/restart and backup/restore exercise during implementation. Prerequisites: A2,B2,B3. Assumptions: single local process and filesystem.

C3 Checkpoint: teacher accepts first version (milestone 3, blocked by C2,D1). Criteria: all user outcomes demonstrated in browser and after restart; source/test evidence and local-use/data handling instructions reviewed. Artifact: working Shelfmate plus verification results and README. Stage-1 limitation: checkpoints are ordinary tickets, no enforcement prevents closing without owner review; record owner's actual acceptance.

Coverage: list/add existing=E1, durability and robustness=A1+B1+D1, find=A2+C1, lend/return=B1+B2+C2, overdue=B3+C2, whole first-version acceptance=D1+C3. One teacher/no pupil use=A1 loopback and all UI/privacy boundaries. Keep tech=all tasks. No unresolved blocking choices; all judgment defaults labelled above.

Setup creates .story, 3 milestones plus default p0, 10 tickets (1 complete, 9 pending), initial snapshot, handover and setup note with coverage/decisions. Governance: create AGENTS.md (purpose, boundaries, stack, architecture, testing, assumptions), RULES.md (TDD for business rules, loan invariants, persistence/error/date/privacy rules), REVIEW.md verbatim provided skill template. No existing governance overwritten. Quality level: Full pipeline because circulation is a business workflow. WRITE_TESTS enabled command npm test; TEST enabled command npm test, established by package script and existing test/books.test.js collected by node --test. BUILD disabled, no build step needed for direct Node/plain assets; VERIFY enabled startCommand npm start readinessUrl http://localhost:3000/books (both established from manifest/server). No installs/tests/build/server runs during setup. Git init and .gitignore additions .story/snapshots/, .story/sessions/, .story/status.json, data/, node_modules/. No issue import, deployment, commit or autonomous execution. Setup package must receive explicit approval before any writes.
STORYBLOQ_PLAN"

item.text: The review identified three details to tighten: recovery after an uncertain disk write, protection against requests from unrelated websites, and removal of pupil labels after return. I’m adding explicit behavior and tests for each, while retaining the book and return records.

/bin/zsh -lc "codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --output-schema '/private/tmp/cc-cpm-w4-t536/onboarding-eval-8VV1xt/home/.agents/skills/story/setup-review-schema.json' - <<'STORYBLOQ_PLAN'
Review id: R2
Independently review this consolidated revised setup plan. Return JSON verdict and findings; use a concise verdict such as pass or revise. Read-only review: no file writes, installations, tests, builds or server runs. Evaluate coverage/fidelity, journeys, boundaries/dependencies, feasibility, safety and acceptance evidence. R1 required explicit uncertain-write reconciliation, same-origin protection and implemented pupil-label retention; these are incorporated below.

Evidence: README Shelfmate school book room claims search/lending already done, but src/books.js only lists/adds books in memory and src/server.js only serves GET/POST /books; user confirmed the missing features must be planned. test/books.test.js has one node:test addition test. package.json declares JS ES modules, no dependencies, start=node src/server.js, test=node --test. No git, .story or governance files. User: one teacher, pupils never use app; find book, lend to pupil, return, overdue list, no loss on restart; keep existing technology and use judgment on other choices.

Proposed assumptions: dependency-free Node/JS with simple HTML/CSS/JS browser UI; single process, teacher's local machine, loopback-only, no remote deployment/accounts; one book record per physical copy. Teacher enters minimal pupil label and due date; editable default 14 calendar days. Overdue means outstanding and due date before local current date. No fines, reservations, reminders, cloud or multiuser work. Pupil label exists only for active loan: automatic removal within successful return transaction, retain book id/loan id/dates/return timestamp for recorded-return persistence. Operation retry ledger must not preserve labels. Old backups may contain labels: document local access restrictions and manual deletion/rotation; no invented automatic backup or retention guarantee for external copies.

Durability contract: acknowledge mutations only after serialized atomic JSON persistence reaches supported durability barrier. Persist operation ids with results for add/lend/return in same transaction so retries cannot duplicate changes. On pre-replacement failure leave current state intact. If replacement may have occurred and subsequent durability confirmation fails, report outcome uncertain (not rollback), stop further mutations, require recovery that reloads/validates disk and reconciles operation id before retry; startup completes the supported durability barrier before accepting mutations. Document filesystem-dependent power-loss limits, never guarantee unsupported durability. Fault-inject before/after replacement and restart/retry. On corrupt data refuse startup without rewriting file; only missing file starts empty. Persist ids and loan schema. Runtime data directory excluded from git.

Local browser boundary: validate Host and exact Origin for mutations, require JSON content type plus same-origin custom request header, reject missing/foreign mutation origin; reject foreign supplied Origin on reads, no permissive CORS. Host allowlist must match configured loopback host/port; safe text rendering, no pupil labels in logs/errors. Tests/API clients supply explicit required headers. No auth or new external service.

Three milestones after default p0 Setup, ten tickets with aliases allocated to real ids after approval. All implementation descriptions below include required fields.

Milestone 1: durable searchable catalogue.
E1 Existing list/add catalogue, COMPLETE by code inspection only. Outcome: current list/add from README and src/books.js/server.js. Scope: current in-memory module and HTTP GET/POST /books. Excludes: search/UI/loans/durability/hardening. Acceptance: source implements addition with ids and listing. Behaviour: existing missing-title throw, recorded as current limitation. Verification: cited source and existing test inspected, no tests run. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: none.
A1 Durable catalogue and safe HTTP API, no blockers. Outcome: added books survive restart (user requirement). Scope: JSON repository, ids, serial transactions, operation-id retry/recovery contract above, HTTP parsing/validation/bounds, loopback/Host/Origin/content-type/header policy, injectable storage. Excludes: loans/UI/accounts. Acceptance: acknowledged addition survives restart, unique ids, malformed input 4xx without crash, rejected cross-site requests, explicit failure/uncertainty with no false rollback, disk corruption preserved, duplicate retried addition prevented. Behaviour: empty catalogue, actionable storage errors, stop writes on uncertain persistence until reconciliation, private error/log output. Verification: node:test HTTP policy/input tests; temp-dir restart/concurrent-write/corruption and fault-injection cases before/after replacement and idempotent retries. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: local single process/filesystem.
A2 Searchable teacher catalogue UI, blocked by A1. Outcome: teacher finds books by title or author and adds copies (README/user). Scope: case-insensitive query filtering and plain browser catalogue/add form using operation ids and required same-origin headers. Excludes: loans/overdue/frameworks. Acceptance: both fields searched, blank query shows all, copy identifiable, newly added copy appears after refresh/restart. Behaviour: labelled keyboard controls, focus, safe rendering, loading/empty/no-results/error/retry; uncertain-save explanation and same operation-id retry, never blindly resubmit with fresh id. Verification: node:test search/API and manual keyboard/browser failure/recovery journey. Prerequisites: A1. Assumptions: plain local browser UI.
C1 Checkpoint: teacher reviews catalogue, blocked by A2. Question: is finding/identifying and adding a copy understandable? Artifact: working catalogue screen. Gates only B2 interaction design, not B1 backend or B3 overdue slice.

item.text:
Shelfmate’s first version will let one teacher find books, lend them to pupils, record returns, and see overdue loans, with records preserved across restarts. It keeps the existing Node.js and JavaScript stack, adding a simple browser interface and local JSON storage.

Proposed defaults: one record per physical copy; an editable 14-day loan period; overdue means due before today; pupil labels removed when books are returned, while return records remain. The app runs locally, without pupil accounts.

The setup package contains **10 tickets across three milestones**, plus Storybloq’s default Setup phase. These labels are provisional:

| Milestone | Ticket and purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Durable catalogue | E1: Existing list/add functionality—complete by source inspection | — |
| | A1: Persistent storage, safe requests, and recovery after failed saves | — |
| | A2: Search and add books through the teacher interface | A1 |
| | C1: Teacher reviews the catalogue interface | A2 |
| Circulation | B1: Persistent lending and return API | A1 |
| | B2: Teacher lending and return controls | B1, A2, C1 |
| | B3: Overdue query and display | B1, A2 |
| | C2: Teacher demonstrates the complete circulation journey | B2, B3 |
| Acceptance | D1: Restart/recovery verification and operating instructions | A2, B2, B3 |
| | C3: Teacher accepts the first version | C2, D1 |

A1 can begin immediately after setup. Checkpoints record your review, but Storybloq does not technically enforce owner approval before their closure.

Approval also covers:

- **Project:** `shelfmate`, Node.js, JavaScript.
- **Tracking:** `.story/`, dependencies, initial snapshot, handover, and setup note.
- **Governance:** new `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, and `REVIEW.md`; previews available.
- **Git:** initialize the repository and ignore runtime data, dependencies, snapshots, sessions, and generated status.

Quality level: Full pipeline, because lending involves business rules and persistent state.

| Stage | Configuration |
|---|---|
| WRITE_TESTS | Enabled: `npm test`—established |
| TEST | Enabled: `npm test`—established |
| BUILD | Disabled—no build step needed |
| VERIFY | Enabled: `npm start`, readiness at `http://localhost:3000/books`—established |

The revised plan includes uncertain-save recovery, protection against cross-site requests, and pupil-label removal. Tests remain planned; none were run during setup.
